title: Modal verbs, infinitives and -ing forms in the passive
intro: Read this before the questions on modal verbs and other verb forms in the passive.

blocks.title: modal + be + past participle
items: **can, could, must, should, may, might, would, will:** modal + **be** + past participle: The door **must be locked**. Tickets **can be bought** online. (Active: You must lock the door.)
**Negative:** The door **mustn't be left** open. Mistakes **shouldn't be made**.
**Question:** modal + subject + be + participle: **Can** tickets **be bought** online?
After a modal the verb be stays in the BASE form: *can been bought* and *can being bought* are wrong.

blocks.title: past modals: modal + have been + past participle
items: The window **must have been broken** during the night.
The work **should have been finished** yesterday. (Active: Someone should have finished the work yesterday.)
**Negative and question:** It **couldn't have been done**. **Could** it **have been done**?

blocks.title: infinitive and -ing form
items: **to be + past participle:** She wants **to be invited**. The form has **to be signed**.
**being + past participle:** He hates **being laughed at**. She left without **being seen**.
After a preposition (without, before, after, of) use **being**: *without to be seen* is wrong.

blocks.body: Say the modal, then ask: now or the past? Now gives **be + participle**. The past gives **have been + participle**.

builds: Continuous and perfect tenses in the passive
